The strongest honest case for buying is thin. The brief shows real participation: 764 buyers on the curve, a low top-3 concentration (8.9%), and a graduation that took 30 minutes, with 125 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation and only 27% of those buys from the top five. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is only -7.9 SOL against 75.6 SOL bought, so the selling is not overwhelming in that window.

But the trend is against it. The coin is down 48% over 30 minutes and 28% over the last 15, sitting 63% below its 30-minute high, with sells exceeding buys in the first post-graduation minutes (sell-to-buy 1.14). The 31% bundle share is a warning sign, and a launch bot was present. Pool depth of 54.7 SOL is shallow enough that a $20 round trip would lose several percent to impact. Nothing here shows demand that will still be present in 30-60 minutes; it shows a coin already in a sustained decline.

Recommendation: no buy. I can't make a case that clears the base rates.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a slow bleed, not a sudden rug. The coin is down 48% over 30 minutes and 63% off its high, and the last 15 minutes show sells (83.4 SOL) outrunning buys (75.6 SOL), net flow of -7.9 SOL, and a -28% return. Sellers (202) nearly match buyers (240), so this is distribution into thin demand, not a dip being absorbed. With a 54.7 SOL pool, a $20 ticket moves price and the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost plus 30-second latency means a bounce must clear that hurdle before it fades. The curve shows 31% bundle share and a 0.55 completer share, which points to launch-bot supply exiting. The name "assless" is a meme with no specific edge. Base rates for random post-graduation buys already run around -20% per trade, and this one is in a falling-knife state. Skip.
